meta.title: Bioprinting of GelMA/PEGDA Hybrid Bioinks for SH-SY5Y Cell Encapsulation: Role of Molecular Weight and Concentration.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: GelMA/PEGDA hybrid bioinks were printed with SH-SY5Y cells for nerve guidance conduits. PEGDA concentration and molecular weight tuned stiffness (about 50-600 kPa), degradation and printability.

formulations.stiffness_note: elastic modulus ~50 kPa (10% GelMA) to 600 kPa (10G+15P700)
formulations.name: 10% GelMA + PEGDA hybrids
formulations.key_outcome: Adding PEGDA slowed degradation and raised stiffness; cells spread in GelMA and 10G+5P700 gels.

evidence.quote: All bioinks were printed using a 25G tapered nozzle (250 µm inner diameter).
The elastic modulus of hydrogels ranges from ≈50 kPa (10G) to 600 kPa (10G+15P700 )
The printability of the bioink was performed using an extrusion‐based bioprinter (BIOX6, CELLINK, Sweden).
